cultural.vision_reason: This is a classic Northwest Coast transformation/articulated-mouth face mask with formline painting, moving eyes, fur whiskers, and a movable cedar mandible — exactly the type of ceremonial mask made and used by Heiltsuk and related Northwest Coast peoples for winter ceremonial dances.

physical.title: mask
physical.summary: Large face mask, mostly of alder, deeply carved with bold, high, pointed cheeks, deep eye sockets, with conical orbs, large long eyebrows, painted formline designs in black, green and red, the paint apparently including mica, a separate mandible of red cedar, and moving eyes, the right eye of yew [reddish in colour], left eye of maple, side whiskers of [black?] bear skin, chin whiskers of [grizzly?] bear skin, ears pegged on, but now both missing, one remaining piece of balene pegged in top. Nails used with spruce gum to attach the skin. The mandible is nailed to face, and has twined 'Z' twist cedar bark, stick and mouth pieces for manipulation of jaw, with twine from jaw to eyeballs so they would move together. Straps of a thick fluffy skin, probably moose, but could also be elk. May well represent a bear face.
